title: United Nations-Nippon Foundation Fellowship on Ocean Affairs and the Law of the Sea (2027 Session)
description: A fully funded, nine-month advanced training fellowship for mid-level government officials and other professionals from developing States who work directly on ocean affairs and the law of the sea (including implementation of UNCLOS and SDG-14), run by the UN Division for Ocean Affairs and the Law of the Sea (DOALOS) in partnership with the Nippon Foundation. Fourteen fellowships are offered for the 2027 session. Phase One runs 24 March-30 June 2027 at UN Headquarters in New York; Phase Two is a six-month research placement (1 July-17 December 2027) at an academic host institution selected to match the fellow's research area -- this listing uses New York, the fixed Phase One location every fellow attends, as the destination, and flags that the Phase Two placement institution varies by fellow. According to the official Fellowship Conditions, the program covers fellows' travel, a monthly stipend, visas, medical clearance, insurance, and housing throughout both phases; the exact stipend figure isn't published on the public call-for-applications pages. Open to applicants aged 25-45 from developing States who hold at least a first university degree. This is a long-running annual program (the 2026 session preceded this one).
org: UN Division for Ocean Affairs and the Law of the Sea (DOALOS) / The Nippon Foundation
visaNote: This is a funded fellowship, not employment; visa arrangements for both the New York and host-institution phases are coordinated as part of the Fellowship Conditions.
